     4	/-!
     5	# Magic Square value-to-parity relations
     6	
     7	This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
     8	the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
     9	total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
    10	supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
    11	incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
    12	of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
    13	six row or column constraints.
    14	
    15	The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
    16	answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
    17	`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The Magic Square game is defined in
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`
    23	and `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:201-222`.  These relations are the
    24	probabilistic input to the rigidity result cited at paper lines 612-652 from
    25	Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    29	
    30	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    33	
    34	noncomputable section
    35	
    36	/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/
    37	
    38	/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
    39	def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → MsType × MsType
    40	  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k))
    41	  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)
    42	
    43	/-- Every question pair in the Magic Square distribution is a directed incidence. -/
    44	theorem ms_support_subset_directed_incidences :
    45	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support ⊆
    46	      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image directedIncidence := by
    47	  intro xy hxy
    48	  have hedge : Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges :=
    49	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
    50	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨ik, _hik, heq⟩
    51	  have heq' :
    52	      ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) = xy ∨
    53	        ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) =
    54	          xy.swap :=
    55	    (Sym2.mk_eq_mk_iff (α := MsType)).mp heq
    56	  rcases heq' with heq' | heq'
    57	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, false), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    58	    simpa [directedIncidence] using heq'
    59	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, true), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    60	    simpa [directedIncidence] using congrArg Prod.swap heq'
    61	
    62	/-- The Magic Square question distribution has at most 36 support points. -/
    63	theorem ms_support_card_le :
    64	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤ 36 := by
    65	  calc
    66	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤
    67	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image
    68	          directedIncidence).card :=
    69	      Finset.card_le_card ms_support_subset_directed_incidences
    70	    _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).card :=
    71	      Finset.card_image_le
    72	    _ = 36 := by norm_num
    73	
    74	/-- A constraint-to-variable incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    75	theorem ms_forward_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    76	    (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∈
    77	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    78	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    79	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    80	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    81	
    82	/-- A variable-to-constraint incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    83	theorem ms_reverse_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    84	    (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i) ∈
    85	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    86	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    87	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    88	  rw [Sym2.eq_swap]
    89	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    90	
    91	/-- Every supported question pair has probability at least `1 / 36`. -/
    92	theorem ms_question_weight_ge {xy : MsType × MsType}
    93	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
    94	    (1 : ℝ) / 36 ≤ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy := by
    95	  have hmemFilter :
    96	      xy ∈ ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
    97	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges) := hxy
    98	  rw [show (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy =
    99	      1 / ((graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card : ℝ) by
   100	    change (Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   101	        ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   102	          Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges)).weight xy =
   103	      1 / (((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   104	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges).card : ℝ)
   105	    rw [Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight, if_pos hmemFilter]]
   106	  apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le
   107	  · exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨xy, hxy⟩
   108	  · exact_mod_cast ms_support_card_le

   110	/-! ## Rejection mass from the game value -/
   111	
   112	/-- The rejection mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   113	noncomputable def rejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   114	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false
   115	
   116	/-- The acceptance mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   117	noncomputable def acceptanceMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   118	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = true
   119	
   120	/-- The rejection mass averaged over the Magic Square question distribution. -/
   121	noncomputable def totalRejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) : ℝ :=
   122	  avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   123	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2
   124	
   125	/-- Acceptance and rejection partition the conditioned answer mass. -/
   126	theorem acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
   127	    acceptanceMass S x y + rejectionMass S x y = 1 := by
   128	  rw [← show (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = 1 by
   129	    exact outcome_weight_sum_eq_one S x y]
   130	  unfold acceptanceMass rejectionMass outcomeEventWeight
   131	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   132	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   133	  intro a _
   134	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   135	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   136	  intro b _
   137	  cases h : msWinPredicate x y a b <;> simp [h]
   138	
   139	/-- The strategy value is the average conditioned acceptance mass. -/
   140	theorem strategy_value_eq_acceptance_mass (S : Strategy msGame) :
   141	    S.value = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   142	      acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2 := by
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	/-- Total rejection mass is exactly one minus the strategy value. -/
   146	theorem total_rejection_mass_eq_one_sub_value (S : Strategy msGame) :
   147	    totalRejectionMass S = 1 - S.value := by
   148	  rw [show S.value = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   149	      acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) by rfl]
   150	  unfold totalRejectionMass
   151	  calc
   152	    avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   153	        rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2) =
   154	        avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   155	          1 - acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := by
   156	      apply avgOver_congr
   157	      intro xy
   158	      linarith [show acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2 + rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 = 1 by
   159	        exact acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass S xy.1 xy.2]
   160	    _ = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun _ => 1) -
   161	        avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   162	          acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := avgOver_sub _ _ _
   163	    _ = 1 - avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   164	        acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := by
   165	      rw [avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (by
   166	        unfold graphDistribution
   167	        apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   168	        refine ⟨(.constraint 0, .var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
   169	        simp [msEdges])]
   170	
   171	/-- Total rejection mass is nonnegative. -/
   172	theorem total_rejection_mass_nonneg (S : Strategy msGame) :
   173	    0 ≤ totalRejectionMass S := by
   174	  unfold totalRejectionMass
   175	  exact avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun xy => outcome_event_weight_nonneg S xy.1 xy.2 _
   176	
   177	/-- Value at least `1 - ε` implies total rejection mass at most `ε`. -/
   178	theorem total_rejection_mass_le (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
   179	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) : totalRejectionMass S ≤ ε := by
   180	  rw [total_rejection_mass_eq_one_sub_value]
   181	  linarith
   182	
   183	/-- Conditioned rejection mass is nonnegative. -/
   184	theorem rejection_mass_nonneg (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
   185	    0 ≤ rejectionMass S x y :=
   186	  outcome_event_weight_nonneg S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false
   187	
   188	/-- A supported conditioned rejection mass is at most 36 times total rejection. -/
   189	theorem rejection_mass_le_thirty_six_mul_total (S : Strategy msGame)
   190	    {xy : MsType × MsType}

   287	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   288	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   289	  intro b _
   290	  by_cases hb : E b
   291	  · simp [hb, sum_outcome_weight_left S x y b]
   292	  · simp [hb]
   293	
   294	/-- Inclusion of answer events implies the corresponding Born-weight inequality. -/
   295	theorem outcome_event_weight_mono {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   296	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   297	    (E F : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] [DecidableRel F]
   298	    (hEF : ∀ a b, E a b → F a b) :
   299	    outcomeEventWeight S x y E ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y F := by
   300	  unfold outcomeEventWeight
   301	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   302	  intro a _
   303	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   304	  intro b _
   305	  by_cases hE : E a b
   306	  · simp [hE, hEF a b hE]
   307	  · simp only [hE, ↓reduceIte]
   308	    split_ifs
   309	    · exact outcome_weight_nonneg S x y a b
   310	    · exact le_rfl
   311	
   312	/--
   313	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   314	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   315	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   316	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   317	-/
   318	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   319	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   320	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   321	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   322	
   323	/--
   324	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   325	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   326	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   327	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   328	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   329	intentionally not asserted here.
   330	-/
   331	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   332	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   333	
   334	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Magic Square value-to-parity relations
     6	
     7	This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
     8	the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
     9	total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
    10	supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
    11	incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
    12	of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
    13	six row or column constraints.
    14	
    15	The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
    16	answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
    17	`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The Magic Square game is defined in
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`
    23	and `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:201-222`.  These relations are the
    24	probabilistic input to the rigidity result cited at paper lines 612-652 from
    25	Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
    26	-/

    28	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    29

    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

    35	
    36	/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/
    37	
    38	/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
    39	def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → MsType × MsType
    40	  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k))
    41	  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)
    42	
    43	/-- Every question pair in the Magic Square distribution is a directed incidence. -/
    44	theorem ms_support_subset_directed_incidences :
    45	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support ⊆
    46	      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image directedIncidence := by
    47	  intro xy hxy
    48	  have hedge : Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges :=
    49	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
    50	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨ik, _hik, heq⟩
    51	  have heq' :
    52	      ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) = xy ∨
    53	        ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) =
    54	          xy.swap :=
    55	    (Sym2.mk_eq_mk_iff (α := MsType)).mp heq
    56	  rcases heq' with heq' | heq'
    57	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, false), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    58	    simpa [directedIncidence] using heq'
    59	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, true), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    60	    simpa [directedIncidence] using congrArg Prod.swap heq'
    61	
    62	/-- The Magic Square question distribution has at most 36 support points. -/
    63	theorem ms_support_card_le :
    64	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤ 36 := by
    65	  calc
    66	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤
    67	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image
    68	          directedIncidence).card :=
    69	      Finset.card_le_card ms_support_subset_directed_incidences
    70	    _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).card :=
    71	      Finset.card_image_le
    72	    _ = 36 := by norm_num
    73	
    74	/-- A constraint-to-variable incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    75	theorem ms_forward_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    76	    (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∈
    77	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    78	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    79	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    80	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    81	
    82	/-- A variable-to-constraint incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    83	theorem ms_reverse_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    84	    (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i) ∈
    85	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    86	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    87	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    88	  rw [Sym2.eq_swap]
    89	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    90	
    91	/-- Every supported question pair has probability at least `1 / 36`. -/
    92	theorem ms_question_weight_ge {xy : MsType × MsType}
    93	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
    94	    (1 : ℝ) / 36 ≤ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy := by
    95	  have hmemFilter :
    96	      xy ∈ ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
    97	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges) := hxy
    98	  rw [show (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy =
    99	      1 / ((graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card : ℝ) by
   100	    change (Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   101	        ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   102	          Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges)).weight xy =
   103	      1 / (((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   104	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges).card : ℝ)
   105	    rw [Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight, if_pos hmemFilter]]
   106	  apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le
   107	  · exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨xy, hxy⟩
   108	  · exact_mod_cast ms_support_card_le

   110	/-! ## Rejection mass from the game value -/
   111	
   112	/-- The rejection mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   113	noncomputable def rejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   114	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false
   115	
   116	/-- The acceptance mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   117	noncomputable def acceptanceMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   118	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = true
   119	
   120	/-- The rejection mass averaged over the Magic Square question distribution. -/
   121	noncomputable def totalRejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) : ℝ :=
   122	  avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   123	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2
   124	
   125	/-- Acceptance and rejection partition the conditioned answer mass. -/
   126	theorem acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
   127	    acceptanceMass S x y + rejectionMass S x y = 1 := by
   128	  rw [← show (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = 1 by
   129	    exact outcome_weight_sum_eq_one S x y]
   130	  unfold acceptanceMass rejectionMass outcomeEventWeight
   131	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   132	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   133	  intro a _
   134	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   135	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   136	  intro b _
   137	  cases h : msWinPredicate x y a b <;> simp [h]
   138	
   139	/-- The strategy value is the average conditioned acceptance mass. -/
   140	theorem strategy_value_eq_acceptance_mass (S : Strategy msGame) :
   141	    S.value = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   142	      acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2 := by
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	/-- Total rejection mass is exactly one minus the strategy value. -/
   146	theorem total_rejection_mass_eq_one_sub_value (S : Strategy msGame) :
   147	    totalRejectionMass S = 1 - S.value := by
   148	  rw [show S.value = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   149	      acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) by rfl]
   150	  unfold totalRejectionMass
   151	  calc
   152	    avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   153	        rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2) =
   154	        avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   155	          1 - acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := by
   156	      apply avgOver_congr
   157	      intro xy
   158	      linarith [show acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2 + rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 = 1 by
   159	        exact acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass S xy.1 xy.2]
   160	    _ = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun _ => 1) -
   161	        avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   162	          acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := avgOver_sub _ _ _
   163	    _ = 1 - avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   164	        acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := by
   165	      rw [avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (by
   166	        unfold graphDistribution
   167	        apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   168	        refine ⟨(.constraint 0, .var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
   169	        simp [msEdges])]

   172	theorem total_rejection_mass_nonneg (S : Strategy msGame) :
   173	    0 ≤ totalRejectionMass S := by
   174	  unfold totalRejectionMass
   175	  exact avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun xy => outcome_event_weight_nonneg S xy.1 xy.2 _

   178	theorem total_rejection_mass_le (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
   179	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) : totalRejectionMass S ≤ ε := by
   180	  rw [total_rejection_mass_eq_one_sub_value]
   181	  linarith

   183	/-- Conditioned rejection mass is nonnegative. -/
   184	theorem rejection_mass_nonneg (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
   185	    0 ≤ rejectionMass S x y :=
   186	  outcome_event_weight_nonneg S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false
   187	
   188	/-- A supported conditioned rejection mass is at most 36 times total rejection. -/
   189	theorem rejection_mass_le_thirty_six_mul_total (S : Strategy msGame)
   190	    {xy : MsType × MsType}
   191	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
   192	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤ 36 * totalRejectionMass S := by

     5	/-!
     6	# Magic Square rigidity
     7	
     8	This stable public facade re-exports the elementary symmetry facts and perfect
     9	strategy construction while retaining the imported rigidity theorem and its
    10	supporting definitions.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source statement is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:228-250`, from
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
    17	
    18	The variable indices below are zero-based: indices 0 and 4 represent the
    19	paper's first and fifth variables, respectively.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The ideal two-qubit projector for one Magic Square output bit. The other
    31	qubit is marginalized by summing the two-qubit Pauli basis projectors. -/
    32	noncomputable def idealMagicBitProj (W : PauliKind) (b : ZMod 2) :
    33	    Op (Fin 2 → ZMod 2) :=
    34	  ∑ e : Fin 2 → ZMod 2, if e 0 = b then pauliProj W e else 0
    35	
    36	/-- The ideal state in `thm:ms-rigidity`: two EPR pairs followed by the
    37	auxiliary bipartite state, in local-player register order. -/
    38	noncomputable def idealMsState {ιA'' ιB'' : Type*}
    39	    [Fintype ιA''] [DecidableEq ιA''] [Fintype ιB''] [DecidableEq ιB'']
    40	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')) :
    41	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    42	      (((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'') × ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')) :=
    43	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState (Fin 2 → ZMod 2)) aux)
    44	
    45	/-- The isometries and auxiliary unit state in the conclusion of
    46	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
    47	structure MsRigidityWitness (S : Strategy msGame) where
    48	  ιA'' : Type
    49	  ιB'' : Type
    50	  [ιA''Fintype : Fintype ιA'']
    51	  [ιB''Fintype : Fintype ιB'']
    52	  [ιA''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA'']
    53	  [ιB''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB'']
    54	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    55	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'')
    56	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    57	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')
    58	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')
    59	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    60	
    61	attribute [instance] MsRigidityWitness.ιA''Fintype
    62	  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''Fintype MsRigidityWitness.ιA''DecidableEq
    63	  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''DecidableEq
    64	
    65	/-- Alice's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
    66	noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
    67	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
    68	  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
    69	    (fun _ b => heteroKron
    70	      (conjIsometry w.φA
    71	        (((S.A (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)) 1)
    72	    (fun _ b => heteroKron
    73	      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιA'')) 1)
    74	    (idealMsState w.aux)
    75	
    76	/-- Bob's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
    77	noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
    78	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
    79	  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
    80	    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
    81	      (conjIsometry w.φB
    82	        (((S.B (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)))
    83	    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
    84	      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιB'')))
    85	    (idealMsState w.aux)
    86	
    87	/-- Alice's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
    88	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
    89	noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
    90	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
    91	  let X := heteroKron
    92	    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
    93	  let Z := heteroKron
    94	    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
    95	  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
    96	    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)
    97	
    98	/-- Bob's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
    99	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   100	noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
   101	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
   102	  let X := heteroKron 1
   103	    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
   104	  let Z := heteroKron 1
   105	    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
   106	  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
   107	    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)
   108	
   109	/-- `thm:ms-rigidity`, imported from Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
   110	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:228-250`, paper
   111	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
   112	
   113	The paper states the Euclidean estimate at scale `sqrt ε` at lines 624--626
   114	and explains the norm conversion and local basis change at lines 650--652. One
   115	universal constant applies to every strategy and nonnegative error parameter. -/
   116	theorem exists_ms_rigidity :
   117	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   118	      ∀ S : Strategy msGame, 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   119	        ∃ w : MsRigidityWitness S,
   120	          ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealMsState w.aux‖ ≤
   121	              C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   122	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   123	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   124	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   125	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   126	          msAnticommutatorDistanceA S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   127	          msAnticommutatorDistanceB S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by

   492	\begin{proof}
   493		Finite field arithmetic over $\F_q$ can be performed in time $\polylog q$, by
   494	  Lemma~\ref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}.
   495		The most expensive step in $\decider^\ld$ is to evaluate a univariate
   496	  polynomial $f: \F_q \to \F_q^k$ at some point $t_u \in \F_q$ that corresponds
   497	  to a point $u \in \F_q^m$, which takes time $\poly(m,d,k,\log q)$.
   498	  The function $L_\Point$ is a projection onto $V_\xpt$, which takes time
   499	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ to compute (it just involves ``zeroing out'' the registers
   500	  outside of $V_\xpt$).
   501	  The functions $L_\ALine$ and $L_\DLine$ require computing a canonical linear
   502	  map, which requires performing Gaussian elimination and can be done in time
   503	  $\poly(m,\log q)$.
   504	
   505	  The Turing-machine description of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ can be
   506	  uniformly computed from the integers $(q,m,d,k)$ expressed in binary; the
   507	  complexity of computing the description comes from describing the parameter
   508	  tuple $\ldparams$, which takes time that is at most polynomial in the bit
   509	  length of $(q,m,d,k)$.
   510	\end{proof}

   512	\subsection{The Magic Square game}
   513	\label{sec:ms}
   514	
   515	We recall the \emph{Magic Square game} of Mermin and
   516	Peres~\cite{mermin1990simple,peres1990incompatible,aravind2002simple}.
   517	The Magic Square game is a simple self-test for EPR pairs (it tests for two of
   518	them). In addition, it allows one to test that a pair of observables
   519	\emph{anticommutes}.
   520	Here we use it as a building block to construct the quantum low-degree test. 
   521	
   522	There are several formulations of the Magic Square game; here we present it as a
   523	\emph{binary constraint satisfaction} game~\cite{cleve2014characterization}.
   524	In this formulation of the game (denoted by $\game_\MS$) there are $6$ linear
   525	equations defined over $9$ variables that take values in $\F_2$.
   526	The variables correspond to the cells of a $3 \times 3$ grid, as depicted in
   527	Figure~\ref{fig:ms}.
   528	Five of the equations correspond to the constraint that the sum of the variables
   529	in each row and the first two columns must be equal to $0$, and the last
   530	equation requires that the sum of the variables in the last column must be equal
   531	to $1$.
   532	
   533	\begin{figure}[ht!]
   534		\begin{center}
   535	    \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.6}
   536			\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
   537				\hline
   538				$x_1$ & $x_2$ & $x_3$ \\
   539				\hline 
   540				$x_4$ & $x_5$ & $x_6$ \\	
   541				\hline
   542				$x_7$ & $x_8$ & $x_9$ \\
   543				\hline
   544			\end{tabular}
   545			\caption{The Magic Square game}
   546			\label{fig:ms}
   547			\end{center}
   548	\end{figure}
   549	
   550	The question set $\type^\ms$ of the Magic Square game is the following:
   551	\begin{equation*}
   552	  \begin{split}
   553	    \type^\msc & = \{ \Constraint_i : i = 1, 2, \ldots, 6\}\;,\\
   554	    \type^\msv & = \{ \Variable_j : j = 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}\;,\\
   555	    \type^\ms & = \type^\msc \cup \type^\msv\;.
   556	  \end{split}
   557	\end{equation*}
   558	The questions $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ correspond to the three row
   559	constraints, the questions $\Constraint_4$, $\Constraint_5$ correspond to the first
   560	two column constraints, and question $\Constraint_6$ corresponds to the third
   561	column constraint.
   562	
   563	In the Magic Square game, the verifier first samples a constraint $\Constraint_i
   564	\in \type^\msc$ uniformly at random, and then samples $\Variable_j$, one of the
   565	three variables in the row or column corresponding to $\Constraint_i$, uniformly
   566	at random.
   567	One player is randomly assigned to be the $\Constraint$ player, and the other is
   568	assigned to be the $\Variable$ player.
   569	The $\Constraint$ player is sent the question $\Constraint_i$ and is expected to
   570	respond with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$,
   571	where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables corresponding to
   572	$\Constraint_i$.
   573	The $\Variable$ player is given question $\Variable_j$ and is expected to
   574	respond with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$.
   575	The players win if the $\Constraint$ player's answers satisfy the equation
   576	associated with $\Constraint_i$, and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   577	More precisely, the verifier samples an edge of the type graph (see Section~\ref{sec:types}) $G^\ms$
   578	in Fig.~\ref{fig:type-graph-ms}, sends one endpoint to a random player, and the
   579	other endpoint to the other player.

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here.    201	\section{The Magic Square game}
   202	% Paper label sec:ms kept for cross-reference fidelity.
   203	\label{sec:ms}
   204	
   205	We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
   206	
   207	\begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
   208		\uses{def:game, def:graph-distribution}
   209		The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.
   210	
   211		The question types are
   212		\begin{align*}
   213			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} &= \{\mathsf{Constraint}_i : i = 1,2,\ldots,6\}\;,\\
   214			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}} &= \{\mathsf{Variable}_j : j = 1,2,\ldots,9\}\;,\\
   215			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ms}} &= \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} \cup \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}\;,
   216		\end{align*}
   217		where $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ denotes the constraint of row $i$ (with variables $x_{3(i-1)+1}, x_{3(i-1)+2}, x_{3(i-1)+3}$), $\mathsf{Constraint}_4$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_5$ denote the constraints of the first two columns, and $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$ denotes the constraint of the third column (with variables $x_{i-3}, x_{i}, x_{i+3}$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$, $i \in \{4,5,6\}$).
   218	
   219		The question distribution is as follows: the verifier samples $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ uniformly from $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$, then samples $\mathsf{Variable}_j$ uniformly among the three variables appearing in the row or column of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; one player, chosen uniformly at random, receives $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and the other receives $\mathsf{Variable}_j$. Equivalently, the verifier samples a uniformly random edge of the bipartite \emph{type graph} $G^{\mathrm{ms}}$ on vertex sets $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$ and $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}$, whose edges are $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{3(i-1)+j}$ for $i,j \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{(i-3)+3(j-1)}$ for $i \in \{4,5,6\}$, $j \in \{1,2,3\}$ ($18$ edges in total, and no self-loops), and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other endpoint to the other player.
   220	
   221		The $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player answers with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$, where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; the $\mathsf{Variable}$ player answers with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$. The players win if and only if the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player's answer satisfies the equation associated with $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   222	\end{definition}
   223

     7	\subsection{Games and strategies}
     8	\label{sec:strat}
     9	
    10	\begin{definition}[Two-player one-round games]
    11	  \label{def:game}
    12	  A \emph{two-player one-round game} $\game$ is specified by a tuple
    13	  $(\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ where
    14	  \begin{enumerate}
    15	  \item $\cal{X}$ and $\cal{Y}$ are finite sets (called the \emph{question
    16	      alphabets}),
    17	  \item $\cal{A}$ and $\cal{B}$ are finite sets (called the \emph{answer
    18	      alphabets}),
    19	  \item $\mu$ is a probability distribution over $\cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$
    20	    (called the \emph{question distribution}), and
    21	  \item $D: \cal{X} \times \cal{Y} \times \cal{A} \times \cal{B} \to \{0,1\}$ is
    22	    a function (called the \emph{decision predicate}).
    23	  \end{enumerate}
    24	\end{definition}
    25	
    26	\begin{definition}[Tensor product strategies]
    27	  \label{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    28	  A \emph{tensor product strategy} $\strategy$ for a game $\game = (\cal{X},
    29	  \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is a tuple $(\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ where
    30	  \begin{itemize}
    31		\item $\ket{\psi}$ is a pure quantum state, i.e.\ a unit vector in $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ for finite
    32	    dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mH_A, \mH_B$,
    33		\item $A$ is a set $\{A^x\}$ such that for every $x \in \cal{X}$, $A^x =
    34	    \{A^x_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_A$, and
    35		\item $B$ is a set $\{B^y\}$ such that for every $y \in \cal{Y}$, $B^y =
    36	    \{B^y_b \}_{b \in \cal{B}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_B$.
    37	\end{itemize}
    38	\end{definition}
    39	
    40	\begin{definition}[Tensor product value]
    41	  \label{def:tensor-product-value}
    42		The \emph{tensor product value} of a tensor product strategy $\strategy =
    43	  (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$  with respect to a game $\game=(\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A},
    44	  \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is defined as
    45	  \begin{equation*}
    46			\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \sum_{x,\, y,\, a,\, b} \, \mu(x,y)\, D(x,y,a,b)\,
    47	    \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^y_b\, \ket{\psi}\;.
    48	  \end{equation*}
    49		For $v\in[0,1]$ we say that the strategy $\strategy$ \emph{passes (or wins)
    50	    $\game$ with probability $v$ if} $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \geq v$.
    51	  The \emph{tensor product value} of $\game$ is defined as
    52	  \begin{equation*}
    53			\val^*(\game) = \sup_\strategy \val^*(\game, \strategy)\;,
    54	  \end{equation*}
    55		where the supremum is taken over all tensor product strategies $\strategy$ for
    56	  $\game$.
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	
    60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game
    64	  $\game$.
    65	\end{remark}
    66	
    67	
    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.

    51	\begin{definition}[Two-player one-round games]\label{def:game}
    52		A \emph{two-player one-round game} $\mathfrak G$ is specified by a tuple $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal A, \mathcal B, \mu, D)$ where
    53		\begin{enumerate}
    54			\item $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ are finite sets, called the \emph{question alphabets},
    55			\item $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are finite sets, called the \emph{answer alphabets},
    56			\item $\mu$ is a probability distribution over $\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y$, called the \emph{question distribution}, and
    57			\item $D \colon \mathcal X \times \mathcal Y \times \mathcal A \times \mathcal B \to \{0,1\}$ is a function, called the \emph{decision predicate}.
    58		\end{enumerate}
    59	\end{definition}
    60	
    61	\begin{definition}[Tensor product strategies]\label{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    62		\uses{def:game, def:povm-conventions}
    63		A \emph{tensor product strategy} $\mathcal S$ for a game $\mathfrak G = (\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal A, \mathcal B, \mu, D)$ is a tuple $(\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ where
    64		\begin{itemize}
    65			\item $\ket{\psi}$ is a pure quantum state, i.e.\ a unit vector in $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ for finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_A$, $\mathcal H_B$,
    66			\item $A$ is a set $\{A^x\}$ such that for every $x \in \mathcal X$, $A^x = \{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ is a POVM on $\mathcal H_A$, and
    67			\item $B$ is a set $\{B^y\}$ such that for every $y \in \mathcal Y$, $B^y = \{B^y_b\}_{b \in \mathcal B}$ is a POVM on $\mathcal H_B$.
    68		\end{itemize}
    69	\end{definition}
    70	
    71	\begin{definition}[Tensor product value]\label{def:tensor-product-value}
    72		\uses{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    73		The \emph{tensor product value} of a tensor product strategy $\mathcal S = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ with respect to a game $\mathfrak G = (\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal A, \mathcal B, \mu, D)$ is
    74		\[
    75			\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G, \mathcal S) = \sum_{x,\,y,\,a,\,b} \mu(x,y)\, D(x,y,a,b)\, \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}\,.
    76		\]
    77		For $v \in [0,1]$ we say that the strategy $\mathcal S$ \emph{passes (or wins) $\mathfrak G$ with probability $v$} if $\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G, \mathcal S) \ge v$. The \emph{tensor product value} of $\mathfrak G$ is
    78		\[
    79			\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G) = \sup_{\mathcal S} \operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G, \mathcal S)\,,
    80		\]
    81		where the supremum is taken over all tensor product strategies $\mathcal S$ for $\mathfrak G$.
    82	\end{definition}
    83	
    84	Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in what follows are tensor product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}; similarly, we refer to $\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G)$ as the \emph{value} of the game $\mathfrak G$.
    85

    87	% by the low individual degree test track (Chapter 2), where it names the strategy format
    88	% specific to that test, so a distinct label is used here; see the following remark.
    89	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]\label{def:projective-strategy-general}
    90		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy.IsProjective}
    91		\leanok
    92		\uses{def:tensor-product-strategy, def:povm-conventions}
    93		A strategy $\mathcal S = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    94	\end{definition}
    95

    97		Definition~\ref{def:projective-strategy-general} is the general notion: a strategy for an arbitrary nonlocal game all of whose measurements are projective. The low individual degree chapters use the same term for the concrete data of a two-prover strategy for the $(m,q,d)$ low individual degree test (Definition~\ref{def:projective-strategy} in Chapter~\ref{chap:test}); that definition is the specialization of the present notion to the question format of that particular test. The two usages occur in disjoint contexts.

+  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=

+    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) :
+    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := by
+  have hsum :
+      (∑ b : G.AnswerB, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
+        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1 := by
+    ext i j
+    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
+      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
+    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
+    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
+        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
+      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
+  calc
+    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
+        (inner ℂ S.ψ
+          (applyOperatorToState
+            (∑ b : G.AnswerB,
+              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
+          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
+    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
+        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1) S.ψ)).re := by
+      rw [hsum]
+    _ = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := rfl
+
+/-- Summing over Alice's answers gives Bob's marginal Born weight. -/
+theorem sum_outcome_weight_left {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) :
+    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := by
+  have hsum :
+      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
+        heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b) := by
+    ext i j
+    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
+      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
+    rw [← Finset.sum_mul]
+    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
+        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
+      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
+  calc
+    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
+        (inner ℂ S.ψ
+          (applyOperatorToState
+            (∑ a : G.AnswerA,
+              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
+          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
+    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
+        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
+      rw [hsum]
+    _ = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := rfl
+
+/-- Every answer event has nonnegative Born weight. -/
+theorem outcome_event_weight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
+    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] :
+    0 ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y E := by
+  unfold outcomeEventWeight
+  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => by
+    split_ifs
+    · exact outcome_weight_nonneg S x y a b
+    · exact le_rfl
+
+/-- An answer event depending only on Alice has its Alice marginal weight. -/
+theorem outcome_event_weight_left_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
+    (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
+    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun a _ => E a) = aliceEventWeight S x E := by
+  unfold outcomeEventWeight aliceEventWeight
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro a _
+  by_cases ha : E a
+  · simp [ha, sum_outcome_weight_right S x y a]
+  · simp [ha]
+
+/-- An answer event depending only on Bob has its Bob marginal weight. -/
+theorem outcome_event_weight_right_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
+    (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
+    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun _ b => E b) = bobEventWeight S y E := by
+  unfold outcomeEventWeight bobEventWeight
+  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro b _
+  by_cases hb : E b
+  · simp [hb, sum_outcome_weight_left S x y b]
+  · simp [hb]
+
+/-- Inclusion of answer events implies the corresponding Born-weight inequality. -/
+theorem outcome_event_weight_mono {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
+    (E F : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] [DecidableRel F]
+    (hEF : ∀ a b, E a b → F a b) :
+    outcomeEventWeight S x y E ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y F := by
+  unfold outcomeEventWeight
+  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
+  intro a _
+  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
+  intro b _
+  by_cases hE : E a b
+  · simp [hE, hEF a b hE]
+  · simp only [hE, ↓reduceIte]
+    split_ifs
+    · exact outcome_weight_nonneg S x y a b
+    · exact le_rfl
+

     4	/-!
     5	# The Magic Square game
     6	
     7	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     8	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
     9	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    10	carrier is needed here.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, from
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    24	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 207-222, paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    26	-/
    27	inductive MsType where
    28	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    29	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    30	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    31	
    32	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    33	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    35	-/
    36	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    37	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    38	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    39	
    40	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    41	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`; paper
    42	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    43	-/
    44	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    45	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    46	
    47	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    48	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    50	-/
    51	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    52	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    53	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    54	
    55	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    56	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    57	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    59	-/
    60	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    61	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    62	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    63	
    64	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    65	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`,
    66	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    67	-/
    68	inductive MsAnswer where
    69	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    70	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    71	  deriving DecidableEq
    72	
    73	/-- A formalization-only total relabeling from the global Magic Square answer
    74	alphabet to a bit. It folds wrong-form answers into zero so that a variable
    75	question yields a complete binary measurement. -/
    76	def msBitOrZero : MsAnswer → ZMod 2
    77	  | .bit b => b
    78	  | .triple _ => 0
    79	
    80	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    81	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    84	-/
    85	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    86	
    87	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    88	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    89	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    93	  toFun
    94	    | .triple β => .inl β
    95	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    96	  invFun
    97	    | .inl β => .triple β
    98	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    99	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   100	  right_inv := by
   101	    intro x
   102	    cases x <;> rfl
   103	
   104	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
   105	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   106	
   107	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   108	
   109	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   110	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 207-222; paper
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   112	-/
   113	def msWinPredicate :
   114	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   115	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   116	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   117	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   118	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   119	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   120	      decide
   121	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   122	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   123	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   124	      decide
   125	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   126	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   127	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   128	
   129	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   132	-/
   133	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   134	  QuestionA := MsType
   135	  QuestionB := MsType
   136	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   137	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   138	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   139	  μ_prob := by
   140	    apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   141	    refine ⟨(.constraint 0, .var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
   142	    simp [msEdges]
   143	  decide := msWinPredicate
   144	
   145	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   512	\subsection{The Magic Square game}
   513	\label{sec:ms}
   514	
   515	We recall the \emph{Magic Square game} of Mermin and
   516	Peres~\cite{mermin1990simple,peres1990incompatible,aravind2002simple}.
   517	The Magic Square game is a simple self-test for EPR pairs (it tests for two of
   518	them). In addition, it allows one to test that a pair of observables
   519	\emph{anticommutes}.
   520	Here we use it as a building block to construct the quantum low-degree test. 
   521	
   522	There are several formulations of the Magic Square game; here we present it as a
   523	\emph{binary constraint satisfaction} game~\cite{cleve2014characterization}.
   524	In this formulation of the game (denoted by $\game_\MS$) there are $6$ linear
   525	equations defined over $9$ variables that take values in $\F_2$.
   526	The variables correspond to the cells of a $3 \times 3$ grid, as depicted in
   527	Figure~\ref{fig:ms}.
   528	Five of the equations correspond to the constraint that the sum of the variables
   529	in each row and the first two columns must be equal to $0$, and the last
   530	equation requires that the sum of the variables in the last column must be equal
   531	to $1$.
   532	
   533	\begin{figure}[ht!]
   534		\begin{center}
   535	    \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.6}
   536			\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
   537				\hline
   538				$x_1$ & $x_2$ & $x_3$ \\
   539				\hline 
   540				$x_4$ & $x_5$ & $x_6$ \\	
   541				\hline
   542				$x_7$ & $x_8$ & $x_9$ \\
   543				\hline
   544			\end{tabular}
   545			\caption{The Magic Square game}
   546			\label{fig:ms}
   547			\end{center}
   548	\end{figure}
   549	
   550	The question set $\type^\ms$ of the Magic Square game is the following:
   551	\begin{equation*}
   552	  \begin{split}
   553	    \type^\msc & = \{ \Constraint_i : i = 1, 2, \ldots, 6\}\;,\\
   554	    \type^\msv & = \{ \Variable_j : j = 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}\;,\\
   555	    \type^\ms & = \type^\msc \cup \type^\msv\;.
   556	  \end{split}
   557	\end{equation*}
   558	The questions $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ correspond to the three row
   559	constraints, the questions $\Constraint_4$, $\Constraint_5$ correspond to the first
   560	two column constraints, and question $\Constraint_6$ corresponds to the third
   561	column constraint.
   562	
   563	In the Magic Square game, the verifier first samples a constraint $\Constraint_i
   564	\in \type^\msc$ uniformly at random, and then samples $\Variable_j$, one of the
   565	three variables in the row or column corresponding to $\Constraint_i$, uniformly
   566	at random.
   567	One player is randomly assigned to be the $\Constraint$ player, and the other is
   568	assigned to be the $\Variable$ player.
   569	The $\Constraint$ player is sent the question $\Constraint_i$ and is expected to
   570	respond with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$,
   571	where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables corresponding to
   572	$\Constraint_i$.
   573	The $\Variable$ player is given question $\Variable_j$ and is expected to
   574	respond with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$.
   575	The players win if the $\Constraint$ player's answers satisfy the equation
   576	associated with $\Constraint_i$, and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   577	More precisely, the verifier samples an edge of the type graph (see Section~\ref{sec:types}) $G^\ms$
   578	in Fig.~\ref{fig:type-graph-ms}, sends one endpoint to a random player, and the
   579	other endpoint to the other player.
   580	
   581	\begin{figure}[!htbp]
   582	  \centering
   583	  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=.8]
   584	
   585	    \tikzset{type/.style args={[#1]#2}{
   586	        draw,circle,fill,scale=0.25,
   587	        label={[font=\scriptsize, label distance=1pt]#1:#2}
   588	      }}
   589	
   590	
   591	
   592	    \foreach \i in {1,...,6} \draw (0,8-9/8*\i)
   593	    coordinate (Constraint-\i)
   594	    node[type={[180]$\Constraint_\i$}] {};
   595	
   596	    \foreach \i in {1,...,9} \draw (2.5,9-\i)
   597	    coordinate (Variable-\i)
   598	    node[type={[0]$\Variable_\i$}] {};
   599	
   600	    \foreach \i in {1,...,3} \foreach \j in {1,...,3}
   601	    \pgfmathsetmacro{\k}{(\i-1)*3+\j}
   602	    \draw (Constraint-\i) -- (Variable-\k);
   603	
   604	    \foreach \i in {4,...,6} \foreach \j in {1,...,3}
   605	    \pgfmathsetmacro{\k}{\i-3+(\j-1)*3}
   606	    \draw (Constraint-\i) -- (Variable-\k);
   607	  \end{tikzpicture}
   608	  \caption{Type graph $G^\ms$ for the Magic Square game.  }
   609	  \label{fig:type-graph-ms}
   610	\end{figure}
   611	
   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}
   653	
   654	We will need the following theorem,
   655	which shows that any pair of anticommuting observables 
   656	can be used to form a value-$1$ strategy for the Magic Square game.
   657	
   658	\begin{theorem}
   659	  \label{thm:ms-from-ac}
   660	  Let $A = \{A_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ and $B = \{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ be two-outcome
   661	  projective measurements acting on $(\C^q)^{\otimes n}$ which are consistent on
   662	  $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n}$, and let $\mathcal{O}_A = A_0 - A_1$ and
   663	  $\mathcal{O}_B = B_0 - B_1$ be the corresponding observables.
   664	  Suppose that $\mathcal{O}_A \mathcal{O}_B = -\mathcal{O}_B \mathcal{O}_A$.
   665	  Then there exists a symmetric strategy $\strategy = (\psi, M)$ for the Magic
   666	  Square game with the following properties.
   667	  \begin{enumerate}
   668	  \item $\strategy$ is an SPCC strategy of value $1$.
   669	  \item The state $\ket{\psi}$ has the form $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes
   670	      n} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}$.
   671	  \item For $b \in \{0,1\}$, we have $M^{\Variable_1}_b = A_b \otimes I$ and
   672	    $M^{\Variable_5}_b = B_b \otimes I$.\label{item:embeds}
   673	  \end{enumerate}
   674	\end{theorem}

/-!
# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value

This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
`Measurement` structure.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/--
A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
-/
structure Game where
  QuestionA : Type
  QuestionB : Type
  AnswerA : Type
  AnswerB : Type
  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool

attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq

/--
The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
  M.postprocess Prod.fst

/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
  M.postprocess Prod.snd

/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)

/--
The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
-/
structure Strategy (G : Game) where
  ιA : Type
  ιB : Type
  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB

attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq

/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
  Matrix.kronecker A B

/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ

/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-48`. -/
noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re

/-- Alice's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
noncomputable def aliceOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (a : G.AnswerA) : ℝ :=
  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1
  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re

/-- Bob's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
noncomputable def bobOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)
  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re

/-- The Born weight of a decidable event on the two answers at fixed questions. -/
noncomputable def outcomeEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] : ℝ :=
  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
    if E a b then outcomeWeight S x y a b else 0

/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Alice's answer. -/
noncomputable def aliceEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, if E a then aliceOutcomeWeight S x a else 0

/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Bob's answer. -/
noncomputable def bobEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (y : G.QuestionB) (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
  ∑ b : G.AnswerB, if E b then bobOutcomeWeight S y b else 0

/-- Every answer-pair Born weight is nonnegative.  This is formalization-only
support for the probability expression in `def:tensor-product-value`. -/
theorem outcome_weight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) :
    0 ≤ outcomeWeight S x y a b := by
  unfold outcomeWeight applyOperatorToState heteroKron
  exact
    (Matrix.isPositive_toEuclideanLin_iff.mpr
      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
        (kronecker_nonneg ((S.A x).pos a) ((S.B y).pos b)))).re_inner_nonneg_right S.ψ

/-- The Born weights of all answer pairs at fixed questions sum to one.  This
is formalization-only support for the POVM normalization implicit in
`def:tensor-product-value`. -/
theorem outcome_weight_sum_eq_one {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) :
    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b = 1 := by
  have hsum :
      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
          (1 : Op (S.ιA × S.ιB)) := by
    ext i j
    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
    simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul]
    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
    exact congrFun (congrFun
      (Matrix.one_kronecker_one (m := S.ιA) (n := S.ιB) (α := ℂ)) i) j
  calc
    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b =
        (inner ℂ S.ψ
          (applyOperatorToState
            (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState 1 S.ψ)).re := by rw [hsum]
    _ = 1 := by
      simp [applyOperatorToState, S.ψ_norm]

/-- Summing over Bob's answers gives Alice's marginal Born weight. -/
theorem sum_outcome_weight_right {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) :
    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := by
  have hsum :
      (∑ b : G.AnswerB, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1 := by
    ext i j
    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
  calc
    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)

paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
The direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the

theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}

      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
      (condLinearConcat L R) := by

/--
The graph distribution samples an ordered endpoint pair whose unordered edge
`s(a,b)` lies in `E`, including self-loops.  It is the inlined graph sampler of
`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:553-563`;
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
The underlying graph-distribution definition is
`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
-/
noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)

/-- The graph sampler has unit mass whenever its edge set is nonempty. -/
theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
  sorry
